styleProfile.corridorCharacter: A pedestrian footbridge viewed from drone altitude crossing over a road or waterway. A lightweight elevated deck 4 meters wide spanning 30-60 meters between abutments. The structure type and material vary by variant — steel truss, cable-stayed, timber-clad, or stress-ribbon. The deck surface is smooth and uninterrupted with handrails or parapets on both sides. Approach ramps or stairs connect to grade at each end.
styleProfile.movementHierarchy: Pedestrian only — slow walking pace with stopping points for views
styleProfile.surfaceType: Deck material varies — steel plate, glass panels, timber planking, or concrete
styleProfile.plantingCharacter: Approach landscaping at abutments — ornamental grasses, groundcover, and small trees framing entry points
styleProfile.edgeConditions: Railing type varies — cable mesh, glass balustrade, timber post-and-rail, or solid parapet wall
styleProfile.publicRealm: Elevated viewpoint and crossing experience — landmark wayfinding element with panoramic sightlines

archetypes.title: Landscape Park Pedestrian Bridge
archetypes.description: Bridge embedded within park or natural landscape, crossing creeks, ponds, ravines, or wetlands. Designed to feel like an extension of the terrain using materials and forms that complement rather than dominate the natural setting.

styleProfile.corridorCharacter: A landscape pedestrian bridge viewed from drone altitude crossing over a creek, pond, or ravine within a park setting. A low-profile deck 3 meters wide sitting close to grade or water level. Natural materials — timber, weathering steel, or planted surface — blending with the surrounding landscape. The bridge reads as a subtle continuation of the park path rather than a dominant structure.
styleProfile.movementHierarchy: Pedestrian only — contemplative walking pace through nature
styleProfile.surfaceType: Deck material varies — rough-sawn timber, concrete with natural aggregate, or planted growing medium
styleProfile.plantingCharacter: Riparian and wetland planting at approaches — native grasses, sedges, wildflowers, and overhanging willows or alders
styleProfile.edgeConditions: Railing type varies — timber post-and-rail, perforated Cor-Ten panels, or no railing on low boardwalks
styleProfile.publicRealm: Immersive nature crossing — intimate proximity to water, wildlife, and landscape

archetypes.title: Dedicated Cycle Bridge
archetypes.description: Bridge designed exclusively for cyclists and micromobility, featuring gentle gradients (max 4-5%), smooth curves with generous radii, and wind-protected profiles. Prioritizes flow and momentum through spiraling ramps or gradual inclines rather than steep approaches.

styleProfile.corridorCharacter: A dedicated cycle bridge viewed from drone altitude crossing over a road, rail corridor, or waterway. A smooth continuous deck 5 meters wide with gentle gradients and sweeping curves. Aerodynamic profile with wind-shielding parapets. Slender structural supports — Y-columns, cable stays, or arches. The deck surface is smooth asphalt or resin-bound aggregate optimized for rolling wheels.
styleProfile.movementHierarchy: Cycling and micromobility only — continuous flow at 20-30 km/h
styleProfile.surfaceType: Smooth asphalt, resin-bound aggregate, or hardwood timber deck
styleProfile.plantingCharacter: Minimal on-bridge planting — approach landscaping with low groundcover and ornamental grasses at ramp bases
styleProfile.edgeConditions: Wind-shielding parapets — perforated metal, glass panels, or solid powder-coated steel
styleProfile.publicRealm: Dynamic elevated cycling experience — flowing movement with panoramic urban views

archetypes.title: Shared Cycle-Pedestrian Bridge
archetypes.description: Wide multi-use bridge carrying both cyclists and pedestrians with physically separated lanes divided by raised curb, planting strip, or level change. Balances generous width for two traffic types with clear wayfinding through surface colour and texture differentiation.

styleProfile.corridorCharacter: A shared cycle-pedestrian bridge viewed from drone altitude crossing over a road, rail, or waterway. A wide deck 7 meters total with physically separated lanes — cycle lane and pedestrian zone divided by a raised curb, planting strip, or level change. Surface colour differentiation clearly marks the two zones. Structural supports vary by variant — concrete box girder, tied arch, cable-stayed, or hybrid truss.
styleProfile.movementHierarchy: Dual mode — cycling at 15-25 km/h and pedestrian walking, physically separated
styleProfile.surfaceType: Differentiated surfaces — smooth asphalt or red-tinted cycle lane, textured concrete or timber pedestrian zone
styleProfile.plantingCharacter: Linear planter strip separating modes where present — ornamental grasses, sedums, or low shrubs. Approach landscaping at abutments.
styleProfile.edgeConditions: Railings on outer edges — galvanized steel, glass panels, or timber balustrades. Central divider — raised curb, bollard lights, or planted strip
styleProfile.publicRealm: Inclusive elevated crossing accommodating both active transport and leisurely walking with clear modal separation
